newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota sees 97/98 exports to U.S. falling slightly.
newsitem.headline: Toyota sees 97/98 exports to U.S. falling slightly.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp said on Tuesday it plans to reduce vehicle exports to the United States to 480,000 units in the current business year to March 1998 from an actual 490,000 a year earlier.
Exports to North America will be lower this year as production at Toyota's North American units will be increased to 850,000 units from 800,000 units a year earlier, a Toyota spokesman said.
The increased output can be mainly attributed to production of new minivans at its Kentucky plant, he said.
In 1997/98, overall vehicle exports by Toyota, Japan's top carmaker, are expected to rise to 1.40 million units from 1.31 million a year earlier, he said.
Exports to Europe are likely to rise to 390,000 units this business year from 310,000 a year earlier, he said.
Overall overseas production will grow to 1.52 million units from 1.38 million a year earlier, he said.

Production in Asia will rise to 340,000 in 1997/98 from 260,000 a year earlier, mainly because full production of the Soluna model has started at Toyota's second plant in Thailand, the spokesman said.
